quick_skim.title: Same Semantics, Different Outcome: On the Modality Robustness of Multimodal LLMs under Knowledge Conflict
quick_skim.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are increasingly provided with contextual evidence in heterogeneous forms: as a text passage, as a rendered image of the same passage, or as both together. However, it remains unclear how consistently these surface forms are processed, especially when the evidence conflicts with the model's parametric knowledge. We study modality robustness under knowledge conflict across 13 MLLMs and two datasets, and find them far from robust. (1) Contrary to common belief, models favor a context that contradicts parametric knowledge more readily in image form than in text form; (2) when a contradicting text and image are presented together, the preferred modality is essentially arbitrary, varying with input order, model, and dataset. We further demonstrate that this instability has practical consequences: it degrades performance in multimodal RAG and can be exploited by adversarial attacks. To alleviate this brittleness, we examine several simple techniques---prompting, steering, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and direct preference optimization; the majority prove ineffective, whereas SFT achieves moderate success. We therefore call for greater awareness of this inconsistency and argue that it is fundamental, demanding attention at multiple training stages.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Analysis of 13 multimodal LLMs under knowledge conflict shows contexts in image form are more readily trusted and that modality preference is often arbitrary, revealing poor modality robustness.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 为了考察多模态大模型在文字和图像证据形式下是否真正稳健，在13个MLLM和两个数据集上研究了与参数知识冲突的证据呈现方式。发现模型对图像形式的反参数上下文比文本形式更轻信，当文本与图像同时出现时择优模态几乎任意，且模型间差异很大。研究揭示多模态上下文一致性不足，提示在融合不同模态时必须关注知识冲突与鲁棒性问题，但对缺失模态或情感识别并未展开。
